newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets pause, consolidate gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets pause, consolidate gains.

text.p: Most European stock markets paused on Thursday morning to consolidate recent record highs, with traders refocusing on corporate earnings now that Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Congressional testimony is complete.

The dollar also slipped below 1.83 marks as Germany's central bank met for the last time before taking a summer recess. Most analysts expected German rates to remain steady but were wary Bundesbank members might try to talk the dollar lower against the mark.
The dollar has lingered near six-year highs against the mark.

"This talk (of the Bundesbank moving to a variable repurchase rate from a fixed rate) has gone around before, but it's highly unlikely we'll see any change at all at the meeting, not before the summer recess," said Tom Rayner, economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
Even if the Bundesbank tries to talk up the mark, traders said the effects would likely be short-lived.
Stocks were mixed, consolidating recent runs to record peaks, but Finnish shares managed to break out to a record high.

Finland's FOX index started cautiously higher but extended gains to a record peak midmorning after telecoms group Ericsson surged about 12 percent on impressive first-half results. Ericsson said pre-tax profits gained 44 percent versus a year ago.

Germany's DAX index, Europe's forerunner in the race this week to all-time highs after Greenspan predicted moderate economic growth amid low inflation this year in the U.S., slid in early bourse trade as banking shares slipped on corporate earnings.

Commerzbank AG and Vereins- und Westbank AG fell after first-half results. By midmorning, Commerzbank was down three marks at 62.00 despite higher-than-expected earnings. Commerzbank said first-half operating profits rose 23.2 percent.
Vereinsbank shares tumbled 14 marks to 101.00 on lower-than-expected earnings. Its operating profit rose 15.2 percent in the first half.
Despite the DAX's slip, traders remained upbeat on the index, saying the dollar's continued strength and Wall Street's higher close overnight would keep the market underpinned.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 26.71 points at 8,088.36.
Dutch shares, which also posted a record high on Wednesday, edged into positive ground with help from strong second-quarter results from Philips Electronics NV.

Philips shares jumped more than eight percent to a year high of 177 after the company said second-quarter net profits from ordinary operations rose to 693 million guilders from a year ago, outpacing analysts' expectations between 429 and 540 million.
French stocks recovered early losses made when investors sold shares to lock-in profits made in this week's jump to record highs.
In London, a smaller-than-expected British May trade deficit boosted the FTSE out of slightly negative ground but bonds stayed steady.
Britain's May global deficit tallied 508 million sterling, sharply lower than April's 989 million and forecasts for 960 million.

The next major news for British traders will come at 1000 GMT, when the Confederation of British Industry reports on industrial trends. Traders will be keen to see how much sterling's recent strength has cost British industries.
CURRENCIES AT 0935 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8275 marks and 115.80 yen compared to 1.8235 and 115.73 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0935 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 20.3 points at 4,894.80.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 32.08 points in bourse trade at 4,374.01.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 8.09 points at 3,011.62.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened lower at $320.15 per ounce from Wednesday's close at $324.75. Silver opened down at $4.28 from the last close at $4.32.
